hashtags.gloss: Literally 'you will not drive' — a slogan associated with the pre-2018 ban on women driving in Saudi Arabia.
Literally 'the Saudi woman drives' — a tag used around the June 2018 date women were first permitted to drive.
General topic tag meaning 'Saudi women's driving' — used across the discourse regardless of the writer's position.
Literally 'the Saudi woman drives the car' — describes the act of driving, used in both supportive and mocking contexts.
Literally 'the King champions women's driving' — a tag framing the decree as a royal initiative/achievement.
Literally 'women driving the car is a necessity' — frames driving as a practical need.
General topic tag meaning 'women driving the car'.
Colloquial/defiant phrase, roughly 'we will drive right over your objections' — used by supporters, informal/slang register.
Literally 'you will drive, and the people are with you' — a supportive/solidarity tag addressed to women.
English-language equivalent tag for the Saudi women's driving topic, often used in tweets aimed at international audiences.
Literally 'society is with women's driving' — frames public opinion as supportive.
Short general topic tag: 'women's driving'.
Literally 'permission for women's driving' — references the decree/permission itself, neutral framing.
Literally 'MBC incites women's driving' — references MBC, a major Saudi/Gulf media network, being blamed by some for promoting the topic.
References the Shura Council (Saudi consultative assembly) rejecting or discussing women's driving — an institutional/political reference, predates the 2018 decree.

Literally 'Saudi women against women's driving' — references a counter-movement of women publicly opposing the change. Note: tweets using this tag may be quoting or mocking the opposing view rather than endorsing it — stance still requires reading the tweet body, not just the tag.
Literally 'women's driving is corruption for society' — an opposition-framed tag, references a conservative religious/social argument against the decree.

Literally 'abolish guardianship' — references the separate Saudi male-guardianship system debate, a related but DISTINCT topic from driving specifically. Can co-occur in the same tweet alongside a driving hashtag (observed in this dataset). A stance on guardianship is not the same as a stance on driving — do not conflate the two.
References the Council of Senior Scholars, Saudi Arabia's top religious authority body — relevant when tweets invoke religious authority on the driving question.
Literally 'thank you Mohammed bin Salman' / 'thank you our King Salman' — direct thanks tags addressed to the Crown Prince or King regarding the decree.
References Saudi driving schools opened to accommodate new women drivers post-decree.
Literally 'Saudi day, world driving day' — a celebratory tag marking the date driving began.
Literally 'women's driving is coming' — anticipatory tag, likely predates implementation.

entities.gloss: Saudi women's rights activist publicly associated with the campaign for women's right to drive.

entities.canonical: محمد بن سلمان (Mohammed bin Salman / MBS)
entities.gloss: Crown Prince of Saudi Arabia; the 2018 royal decree permitting women to drive was issued under his de facto leadership.
King of Saudi Arabia; formal issuer of the royal decree. Note: 'الملك' (the King) alone is ambiguous and may not always refer to Salman specifically — verify from context.
Title 'Crown Prince' — in this period's tweets, typically co-refers to Mohammed bin Salman.

entities.canonical: هيئة كبار العلماء (Council of Senior Scholars)
entities.gloss: Saudi Arabia's highest religious authority body; sometimes invoked in tweets discussing religious permissibility of women driving.
Saudi Arabia's consultative assembly; referenced in tweets about official/legislative discussion of the driving question.
